# P0 derived datasets

## Files generated by the P0 script

Run from repository root:

```bash
python 06_S0_Calculation/p0_vkt_propulsion_scenarios.py
```

- `P0_private_VKT_propulsion_scenarios.csv`: low/central/high assumed PHEV share scenarios, with counts, per-vehicle annual VKT, total VKT, VKT shares, and 1-million-person scaling.
- `P0_bus_propulsion_VKT_estimates.csv`: bus fleet composition estimates, electric-bus per-vehicle VKT annualization, BEV VKT estimate, and unallocated non-BEV VKT residual.

## Private passenger-car baseline

Official Beijing 2023 counts:
- Private passenger vehicles: 5,073,000.
- New-energy private passenger vehicles: 528,000.
- Non-NEV remainder: 4,545,000.

VKT activity anchors:
- 2023 private-car daily travel intensity: 28.4 vehicle-km/day; the model annualizes this to 10,366 km/vehicle-year as the all-private-car activity anchor.
- Private BEV 2023-10: 9.2 charging sessions/month × 169.6 km/session = 1,560.32 km/month; annualized ×12 = 18,723.84 km/vehicle-year. This is an annualized one-month indicator, not a full-year odometer mean.
- Private PHEV: Shanghai 2018 GPS sample mean 14,774.95 km over the annual observation window; this is a cross-city proxy, not a Beijing observation.

The ICE/non-NEV annual VKT is calculated as a residual so the three propulsion classes reconcile to the all-private-car activity anchor:

`D_ICE = (N_private × D_all - N_BEV × D_BEV - N_PHEV × D_PHEV) / N_ICE`

The BEV/PHEV split of Beijing's 528,000 private NEVs is not officially published in the available source. Scenarios use PHEV shares of 10%, 23.96%, and 30%. The 23.96% central proxy is the complement of the national 2023 BEV stock share (76.04%) and is not a Beijing-specific measured split.

## Bus baseline

- Total public-bus category fleet: 23,385 vehicles.
- Total public-bus category annual VKT: 1.151 billion km.
- Beijing Bus Group 2023 social-responsibility report: 16,832 new-energy buses; clean-energy plus new-energy share 94.7%.
- Official Beijing municipal reply in December 2023: 217 hydrogen fuel-cell buses.
- Non-hydrogen new-energy buses are estimated as 16,832 - 217 = 16,615; treated as BEV/electric-drive proxy pending exact year-end fuel-type table.
- Clean-energy aggregate is estimated from the reported 94.7% combined share; CNG/LNG split is unavailable.
- Other bus count is a residual and is not assigned to diesel alone.
- 2023-10 electric-bus monthly VKT 3,770.8 km/vehicle; annualized ×12 = 45,249.6 km/vehicle-year.
- Estimated BEV/electric-drive VKT = 16,615 × 45,249.6 = 751.8 million km/year.
- Residual non-BEV VKT = 1.151 billion - 751.8 million = 399.2 million km/year. This residual is not split among hydrogen, CNG, LNG, diesel, hybrid, or trolleybus.

## Use restrictions

These are competition-ready scenario inputs, not a substitute for an unavailable official 2023 propulsion-by-fuel cross-tab. Keep the evidence class and caveats when copying values into the model.


## Electric-bus electricity estimate

The 2023-10 electric-bus sample reports 2,361.3 kWh/vehicle/month. Annualized to 28,335.6 kWh/vehicle-year and multiplied by the provisional 16,615 non-hydrogen new-energy bus count, the fleet electricity estimate is 470.8 GWh/year. For a 1-million-person city under linear population scaling, this is approximately 21.54 GWh/year. This is a one-month annualization and the meter boundary (vehicle-side versus purchased/grid-side) must be confirmed before emissions calculations.

Sensitivity inputs are tabulated in `P0_VKT_intensity_sensitivity.csv`, including historical private-car means, 2022/2023 private-BEV annualizations, Shanghai PHEV quartiles, and the Beijing PHEV daily-VKT cross-check.
